name: Giuoco Pianissimo
idea: Build your position before opening the centre.
notes: Take space in the centre and open a diagonal for your bishop.
Black claims an equal share of the centre.
Develop a knight with a threat against e5.
Black develops and defends the central pawn.
The Italian bishop arrives. Its diagonal points towards f7, guarded only by the king.
Black's bishop mirrors yours. Both sides can develop naturally.
Prepare d4. You can decide when to open the centre.
Black attacks e4 while developing a knight.
Support e4. The central break can wait until your pieces are ready.
Black supports e5 and opens a path for the other bishop.
Get your king safe and bring the rook towards the centre.
Both kings are safe. Next, bring another piece into the game: Re1 or Nbd2 supports your buildup.

challenge.prompt: Your king is safe. Improve another piece.
challenge.hint: Activate the f1-rook or develop the b1-knight towards d2.
challenge.explanation: Your pieces are joining the centre. Keep preparing d4 rather than rushing the attack.

name: Centre Attack
idea: Challenge e5 and open lines for your pieces.
notes: Take space in the centre and open a diagonal for your bishop.
Black claims an equal share of the centre.
Develop a knight with a threat against e5.
Black develops and defends the central pawn.
The Italian bishop arrives. Its diagonal points towards f7, guarded only by the king.
Black develops the bishop to its active diagonal.
This pawn supports the coming d4 push.
Black develops with an attack on e4.
Strike now. The central pawns give you space, but development matters too.
Black exchanges in the centre.
Recapture with the c-pawn and keep a strong central presence.
A check interrupts your development. You must answer it.
Block the check and offer a bishop exchange.
Black trades bishops with check. Recapturing with your queen or b1-knight answers the check; the knight also develops.

challenge.prompt: You’re in check. Recapture and keep developing.
challenge.hint: Your b1-knight can recapture on d2; your queen can too.
challenge.explanation: You answered the check and recovered the bishop. Keep the centre supported as your remaining pieces come out.

name: Two Knights Defence
idea: Meet an active defence with a solid centre.
notes: Take space in the centre and open a diagonal for your bishop.
Black claims an equal share of the centre.
Develop a knight with a threat against e5.
Black develops and defends the central pawn.
The Italian bishop arrives. Its diagonal points towards f7, guarded only by the king.
The second knight comes out and attacks e4. This is the Two Knights Defence.
Defend e4. You choose a quieter game instead of the sharp Ng5 lines.
Black develops the bishop and prepares to castle.
Protect your king before starting anything ambitious.
Black supports the centre.
Keep the d4 break in reserve while completing development.
The position resembles a quiet Italian. Re1 or Nbd2 continues your plan without forcing matters.

challenge.prompt: Keep building. Where should your next piece go?
challenge.hint: The rook can support e4 from e1, or the b1-knight can develop to d2.
challenge.explanation: An active defence does not force a wild game. Finish developing, then choose the right moment for d4.

name: Evans Gambit
idea: Give a pawn to gain time and open the centre.
notes: Take space in the centre and open a diagonal for your bishop.
Black claims an equal share of the centre.
Develop a knight with a threat against e5.
Black develops and defends the central pawn.
The Italian bishop arrives. Its diagonal points towards f7, guarded only by the king.
The bishop on c5 becomes a target for your next idea.
Offer the b-pawn. You want time to develop, not an immediate material return.
Black accepts. You are a pawn down, so make the extra time count.
Attack the bishop while preparing d4.
The bishop retreats but keeps an eye on your king.
Open the centre while your pieces have active routes into the game.
Black takes another pawn. Castling now moves your king off the bishop's diagonal and frees the rook.

challenge.prompt: You’ve opened the centre. Secure your king.
challenge.hint: Castle kingside: move your king from e1 to g1.
challenge.explanation: Your king is safe and your rook can join the attack. The gambit is about active pieces and open lines.
